statement: The weighted arithmetic mean $\bar{x}$ of data points $x_1, \dots, x_n$ with weights $w_1, \dots, w_n$ is defined by $\bar{x} = \frac{\sum_{i=1}^{n}\left(x_{i}\cdot w_{i}\right)}{\sum_{i=1}^{n}w_{i}}$. When weights are inverse variances $w_i = 1/\sigma_i^2$, it is expressed as $\bar{x} = \frac{\sum_{i=1}^{n}\left(\frac{x_{i}}{\sigma_{i}^{2}}\right)}{\sum_{i=1}^{n}\frac{1}{\sigma_{i}^{2}}} = \sigma_{\bar{x}}^{2}\sum_{i=1}^{n}\frac{x_{i}}{\sigma_{i}^{2}}$.

symbols.meaning: weighted arithmetic mean of the observations
value of observation or data point i
normalized weight assigned to observation i (weights summing to 1)
standard error of the weighted mean

properties.property: If all weights are equal, the weighted arithmetic mean is identical to the ordinary arithmetic mean.
properties.why: A constant weight factors out of the numerator and denominator sums, leaving the simple average.

properties.property: For normalized weights summing to one, the expected value of the weighted sample mean is $E(\bar{x}) = \sum_{i=1}^n w'_i \mu_i$, which equals $\mu$ when all observations share a common mean $\mu_i = \mu$.
properties.why: Expectation is linear over the weighted sum of random variables.

properties.property: Under inverse-variance weights $w_i = 1/\sigma_i^2$, the standard error of the weighted mean is $\sigma_{\bar{x}} = \sqrt{\frac{1}{\sum_{i=1}^n \sigma_i^{-2}}} = \sqrt{\frac{1}{\sum_{i=1}^n w_i}}$.
properties.why: It follows as a special case of the variance formula for a linear combination of independent variables.

properties.property: The weighted mean with inverse-variance weights is the maximum likelihood estimator of the common mean for independent, normally distributed variables.
properties.why: Inverse-variance weighting corresponds to the normal distribution log-likelihood optimum.

properties.property: When all observation variances are equal to $\sigma_0^2$, the variance of the inverse-variance weighted mean reduces to $\sigma_{\bar{x}}^2 = \sigma_0^2 / n$.
properties.why: The sum of identical inverse variances simplifies to $n / \sigma_0^2$.

assumptions.assumption: The sum of the weights is non-zero ($\sum_{i=1}^n w_i \neq 0$).
assumptions.breaks_when: All weights are zero or sum to zero, leading to division by zero.

assumptions.assumption: When using inverse-variance weights $w_i = 1/\sigma_i^2$, each variance is strictly positive ($\sigma_i^2 > 0$).
assumptions.breaks_when: Any observation has zero variance ($\sigma_i = 0$), resulting in undefined or infinite weights.

failure_modes.signature: Undefined or indeterminate expression (0/0 or division by zero) when evaluating $\bar{x}$.
failure_modes.cause: The denominator $\sum_{i=1}^n w_i$ is equal to zero.
One or more observations have standard deviation $\sigma_i = 0$ in inverse-variance weighting.
